I have too many passwords to remember these days.
Every website wants a different one, with different rules.
I always tell myself I will write them down properly one day.
Last week, I needed to pay a bill online before it became late.
I opened the website and typed in my usual password quickly.
The screen showed a red message saying it was wrong.
I tried again, typing more carefully this time around.
The same red message appeared right away.
I tried a third time, and it still didn't work at all.
I started to feel a little frustrated with the whole situation.
I tried every password I could remember from the past few years.
None of them worked for this particular website, of course, which somehow made it even more annoying.
I clicked the button that said "forgot password" near the bottom.
The website asked for my email, and I typed it in slowly.
A message said a reset link would arrive soon in my inbox.
I checked my email, but nothing appeared there at all.
I waited five minutes, then ten minutes more.
I refreshed my inbox again and again, but still nothing came through.
I checked my spam folder, just in case it landed there.
There it was, sitting quietly among old advertisements.
I clicked the link right away before it could disappear again somehow.
The website asked me to create a brand new password immediately.
It needed a capital letter, a number, and a special symbol.
I typed something I thought I would remember easily this time.
I saved the new password in my phone this time, in a simple notes app.
I told myself this would be different from all the other times before.
This password would not get lost, I promised myself, standing firmly by that decision.
I paid the bill, finally, almost thirty minutes after I started this whole process.
What should have taken two minutes took much longer than I expected it to.
Still, I felt a small sense of victory when it was finally done, like I had won a tiny, pointless battle.
A week later, I needed to log in again for something small and simple.
I opened my notes app immediately, without any panic this time.
For once, my own careful plan actually worked exactly as intended.
I felt proud of myself for the first time all week over something so small.
